items.title: 6. Discussion
items.text:
The discussion will address:

  • What patterns were identified?
  • How do population and infrastructure relate?
  • Which stations are unusual?
  • What geographic factors might explain the results?
  • What are the main methodological limitations?
  • What does the analysis measure?
  • What does it not measure?

A clear distinction will be maintained between spatial infrastructure availability and actual travel accessibility.

items.title: 1.1 Background
items.text:
The Netherlands has a dense and interconnected transport environment involving railways, cycling, roads, and public transport.

Railway stations operate within this wider geographic environment. Their surrounding populations and transport infrastructure can differ considerably.

GIS provides a way to measure and compare these spatial differences.

items.title: 1.2 Research question
items.text: Which Dutch railway stations have the strongest multimodal environment for the population they serve?

items.title: 1.3 Objectives
items.text:
• Build a reproducible geospatial dataset of Dutch railway stations.
  • Measure population and transport infrastructure around each station.
  • Compare stations across the Netherlands.
  • Identify spatial patterns.
  • Communicate the results through maps and a GIS report.

items.title: 1.4 Scope
items.text:
• Study area: Netherlands
  • Unit of analysis: Railway station
  • Catchment: 1 km circular buffer

Included:

  • Population
  • Cycling infrastructure
  • Major roads
  • Public-transport stops
  • Waterways as geographic context

Excluded from Phase 1:

  • Routing
  • Travel-time analysis
  • Network analysis
  • Passenger flows
  • PostGIS
  • FastAPI
  • Leaflet
  • React

items.title: 2. Literature review
items.text:
The literature review will investigate:

  • Multimodal transportation
  • Railway station catchments
  • Cycling and railway integration
  • Public transport accessibility
  • GIS-based transport analysis
  • Spatial accessibility and proximity measures

The literature will be used to justify the methodology and support interpretation of the results.

items.title: 4.1 Coordinate reference system
items.text:
All spatial calculations will use:

EPSG:28992 — Amersfoort / RD New

items.title: 4.2 Station catchment
items.text:
A 1 km circular buffer will be created around each railway station.

The same catchment will initially be used for all primary metrics.

items.title: 4.3 Population
items.text:
The project will use the CBS 100 m population grid.

Population will be aggregated using the centroid-in-buffer method. A population grid cell contributes to a station when its centroid falls inside the station's 1 km catchment.

Limitation: a cell can partially overlap the catchment while its centroid falls outside it.

items.title: 4.4 Cycling infrastructure
items.text:
Measure the total length of qualifying cycling infrastructure within 1 km of each station.

Metric: cycling_km_1km

The exact OpenStreetMap tagging rules will be documented during data preparation.

items.title: 4.5 Roads
items.text:
Measure the total length of primary, secondary, and tertiary roads within 1 km of each station.

Metric: road_km_1km

items.title: 4.6 Public transport
items.text:
Count public-transport stops within 1 km of each railway station.

Metric: pt_stops_1km

items.title: 4.7 Station-level dataset
items.text:
The final analytical dataset will contain, at minimum:

  • station_id
  • station_name
  • population_1km
  • cycling_km_1km
  • road_km_1km
  • pt_stops_1km
  • geometry

items.title: 4.8 Classification
items.text: To be determined after inspecting the data distributions. The classification method will not be selected until the metrics have been calculated and examined.

items.title: 4.9 Validation
items.text:
The analysis will check:

  • duplicate stations
  • missing geometries
  • invalid geometries
  • CRS consistency
  • unmatched spatial joins
  • missing values
  • invalid or suppressed population values

items.title: Definition of done
items.text:
Phase 1 is complete when:

  • Data sources are documented.
  • The methodology is documented.
  • All spatial calculations use EPSG:28992.
  • The prototype works.
  • The national dataset has been processed.
  • Data-quality checks have been completed.
  • Metric distributions have been examined.
  • A classification method has been justified.
  • Final maps have been produced.
  • The report is complete.
  • The GitHub repository is reproducible.
  • The public article has been published.
